title: Health stocks up, tech stocks down on Friday
summary: On the last trading day of the week, healthcare companies on the Nasdaq rose about 2.1% on average, while technology companies slipped about 0.6%.
why: When money moves from one group of stocks to another, people call it a rotation. One day is not a trend, but if it keeps happening, our tech-heavy companies could lag while health companies like Eli Lilly do better.

title: TSMC's sales jumped 55% in a year
summary: TSMC, the factory that builds chips for NVIDIA, AMD and Apple, reported September sales of about NT$512 billion, 54.6% more than a year earlier. Sales for the first nine months of 2026 grew about 41%.
why: TSMC builds the chips that power AI. When its sales keep growing this fast, it means companies are still buying lots of AI chips, which is good news for the AI suppliers on our list.

title: The Fed may raise interest rates again
summary: Notes from the Federal Reserve's last meeting showed most officials expect another rate increase this year, because prices are still rising about 3.4% a year, well above their 2% goal. The Fed already raised rates in September.
why: Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive and make safe savings pay more. That can pull money away from stocks, especially fast-growing companies that look expensive, like many AI stocks.

title: Coming up: the Fed decides on rates Oct. 28-29
summary: The Federal Reserve's next meeting is October 28-29. According to the same report, traders expect the Fed to wait at that meeting and raise rates in December.
why: Fed meeting days often make the whole market jumpy. A surprise in either direction can move every stock on our list.

title: Rocket Lab's big new rocket might slip to 2027
summary: Rocket Lab said the window to launch its larger Neutron rocket before the end of 2026 is narrowing, and a filing said the first flight could slip into 2027. A fuel tank broke during a test in January, which already caused a delay.
why: Investors are paying today for rockets Rocket Lab plans to fly tomorrow. Delays push back the money those launches would earn, which is one reason the stock is far below its high.

title: Inflation report due Wednesday
summary: The government will publish September price numbers on Wednesday, Oct. 14. Forecasters expect yearly inflation to rise to about 3.6%, up from 3.4% in August, mostly because gasoline prices were very high. Until the real number comes out, this is only a guess.
why: Inflation is how fast prices go up. If it is higher than people expect, the Fed may keep interest rates high or raise them, and that usually makes stocks that cost a lot compared with their profits, like AMD, fall more.

title: Coming up: the Fed decides on rates Oct. 27-28
summary: Minutes from the Fed's last meeting showed that officials expect another rate increase may be needed this year. The next decision is at the end of October.
why: The Fed sets the rate banks charge each other, and that moves what everyone pays to borrow. Higher rates usually make bonds look better and can pull stock prices down.

title: Microsoft reportedly plans its own AI chip
summary: Press reports say Microsoft plans to show a new chip called Maia 300 and has talked with TSMC about making hundreds of thousands of them for 2027. Microsoft has not confirmed the timing, and reports disagree on when it will arrive.
why: If big companies build their own chips, they may buy fewer from NVIDIA over time. But TSMC would likely make the chips either way, so this is something to watch, not a sure thing.

title: TSMC will report its results on Thursday
summary: TSMC, the world's biggest maker of advanced chips, will share its July to September results on Thursday, Oct. 15, at 2:00 am Eastern time. Its own forecast for the quarter was sales of about $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion.
why: TSMC builds chips for NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom. If it says orders are strong, that is a good clue for those companies too; if it sounds careful, they can fall together. A forecast is not a result, so wait for the real numbers.

title: Meta shares rise after new AI model launch
summary: Meta stock climbed about 2.6% on Tuesday, adding to a jump on Monday. Reports link the rise to the company's new AI models and to analysts raising their price targets. We could not open the article, so the details come from a search summary.
why: Investors pay more for a company when they believe its new products will earn money. But a stock that has already jumped has less room to rise if the news turns out to be smaller than hoped.

title: Inflation report due Wednesday morning
summary: The September consumer price report comes out on Oct. 14 at 8:30 am Eastern. Economists polled by Dow Jones expect prices to rise 0.6% in the month and 3.6% over the past year, helped by higher energy costs. The Fed's next meeting is Oct. 27 and 28.
why: Inflation is how fast prices rise. If it is hotter than expected, investors may think interest rates will stay high or go up, which can pull down stocks that already cost a lot compared with their profits.

title: TSMC reports record sales for July to September
summary: The Taiwanese chipmaker said its sales for the third quarter were about 50% higher than a year before and above what analysts expected. It did not give an outlook yet. That comes with its full earnings report on Thursday, Oct. 15.
why: TSMC builds chips for many AI companies, so strong sales suggest those customers are still buying. The outlook it gives on Thursday matters even more than last quarter's numbers.

title: Eli Lilly slips about 1.3% on Tuesday
summary: Shares of the drugmaker dipped to about $1,167 in lighter than normal trading. The article notes that analysts still lean positive, and also points to questions about how many people stopped taking an experimental weight loss drug in a trial.
why: Drug company shares often move on trial results, since a medicine's success drives future sales. A small dip on low volume is usually not a big signal by itself.

title: Inflation rises to 3.7% as gasoline jumps
summary: Consumer prices in September were 3.7% higher than a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August and a bit above the 3.6% economists expected. Prices rose 0.6% in the month, with gasoline up 9.1% making up about half of that. Without food and energy, prices rose 0.3% in the month and 2.6% over the year.
why: Inflation is how fast prices go up. When it speeds up, people expect the Fed to keep interest rates high or raise them, and that tends to push down stocks that already cost a lot compared with what they earn.

title: Hot inflation report drags tech and chip stocks lower
summary: Wall Street ended lower on Wednesday after the inflation numbers. The Nasdaq lost about 1.9% and the S&P 500 about 1%, with chip stocks leading the way down and NVIDIA off more than 3%.
why: Chip companies are often priced for fast growth far in the future. When interest rates look likely to stay high, that future money is worth less today, so these shares tend to fall more than the rest of the market.

title: TSMC reports earnings on Thursday
summary: The Taiwanese chipmaker will share its full results on Oct. 15. Earlier this month it said its July to September sales were a record, about 50% above a year before and above what analysts expected. Investors now want to hear its plan for the coming months.
why: TSMC builds chips for many AI companies. What it says about future orders hints at how much those customers expect to sell, so its outlook can move many stocks on your list.

title: TSMC reports earnings today
summary: The Taiwanese chipmaker shares its full results today, Oct. 15. Earlier this month it said its July to September sales were a record, about 50% above a year before and above what analysts expected. Investors now want to hear its plan for the coming months.
why: TSMC builds chips for many AI companies. What it says about future orders hints at how much those customers expect to sell, so its outlook can move many stocks on your list.

title: TSMC beats forecasts and guides higher
summary: The chipmaker said July to September earnings per ADR share were $4.60, above the $4.45 analysts expected, with sales of about $46.5 billion. Its filing also points to October to December sales of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion. Even so, its shares and other chip stocks ended the day lower.
why: TSMC makes chips for many AI companies, so strong orders hint that its customers expect to sell a lot. Stocks can still fall on good news when investors hoped for even more.
source: TSMC Form 6-K (SEC) and FMP earnings data

title: Three of your companies report next week
summary: Market calendars list GE Aerospace for Oct. 20, Meta for Oct. 21 and Lockheed Martin for Oct. 22. Analysts expect earnings of about $2.00, $6.74 and $7.52 per share. Company dates can still change.
why: An earnings report is a company's report card for three months. If results beat or miss what analysts expected, the share price can jump or drop quickly.

title: A mixed day: Eli Lilly up, Rocket Lab down
summary: Eli Lilly gained 3.5% and Lockheed Martin 2.0%, while Rocket Lab lost 6.6%. The broad S&P 500 fund rose 0.3%. Stocks in different industries often move in different directions on the same day.
why: This is why owning a mix of companies can smooth the ride. When one part of the portfolio falls, another part may rise.

title: Government bond yield sits at its highest in a year
summary: The average yield on 10 year US Treasury bonds was 4.99% in September, up from 4.06% in October 2025. It has risen from 4.13% in February.
why: A bond yield is the interest the government pays you for lending it money. When that safe interest goes up, investors can ask for more before they buy riskier things like stocks, so high yields can weigh on share prices.
source: Alpha Vantage (10 year Treasury constant maturity, monthly)

title: GE, Meta and Lockheed report results next week
summary: GE Aerospace reports on Oct 20, Meta on Oct 21 and Lockheed Martin on Oct 22. Analysts expect earnings per share of about $2.01, $6.67 and $7.52.
why: An earnings report shows if a company made more or less money than experts guessed. A stock can drop even after good news if people hoped for more, so these days are often bumpy.

title: Big tech reports land the week of Oct 26
summary: Microsoft and Alphabet are scheduled to report on Oct 28, and Amazon on Oct 29. Analysts expect about $4.72, $3.02 and $1.96 in earnings per share.
why: These three run huge cloud and AI businesses, so their numbers show how much companies are really spending on AI. That can move the chip makers that sell to them too.

title: Drug and defense shares rise as chips fall
summary: Eli Lilly closed up 3.5% at $1,251.61, about 3% under its 52 week high of $1,292.65. Lockheed Martin gained 2.0% and Intuitive Surgical 1.8%, while Vertiv and NVIDIA fell.
why: Money moves between industries all the time. When chip stocks fall, some investors shift to steadier areas such as medicine and defense, which shows why holding different kinds of companies can smooth the ride.

title: Tech selloff drags the market lower on Friday
summary: US stocks fell on Friday as big technology companies kept sliding. The S&P 500 lost about 1.1% and the Nasdaq about 2%, and chip makers were hit hard as worries grew about how long the AI building boom can last. The Nasdaq ended the week down roughly 4.5%, its worst week since late June.
why: When investors get nervous about one hot idea, like AI chips, many stocks tied to it fall together. That is why owning companies from different industries can make the ride smoother. A bad day or week is common and does not say what happens next.

title: Long term US government bond yield stays near 5.1%
summary: The yield on the 10 year Treasury was reported near 5.1% on Friday, slightly lower on the day. Our own monthly data show the September average at 4.99%, up from 4.06% a year earlier.
why: A bond yield is the interest the government pays you for lending it money. When safe bonds pay more, stocks have to look more attractive to compete, so high yields can push share prices down, especially for fast growing tech companies.

title: Core inflation comes in hotter than expected
summary: The latest US consumer price report showed core inflation, which leaves out food and energy, rising faster than analysts expected. Coverage says this raises the chance that the Federal Reserve raises interest rates again at its meeting at the end of October.
why: Inflation means prices keep rising. To cool it, the Fed can raise interest rates, which makes borrowing more expensive and can slow companies down. Markets often drop when rate hikes look more likely.

title: Lockheed Martin will report quarterly results on October 22
summary: The company announced it will publish its third quarter results before the market opens on Thursday, October 22, with a webcast at 8:30 a.m. Eastern time. Its stock rose 3.7% on Friday ahead of the report.
why: An earnings report shows how much a company really sold and earned. Stocks often move a lot on report day, up or down, depending on whether results beat what analysts expected.

title: Fed meets October 27 and 28 as rate hike odds swing
summary: After the hot inflation report, traders raised their bets that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates again at its next meeting on October 27 and 28. Reports disagree on how likely that is, with estimates ranging from about one in five to about one in two. The 10 year Treasury yield was reported above 5%.
why: The Fed's rate decision changes what banks, companies and families pay to borrow. When rates go up, safe bonds pay more and stocks, especially fast growing tech ones, can look less attractive. Nobody knows the decision in advance, so the weeks before it are often bumpy.

title: Tech rebounds from last week's sell-off
summary: Stocks climbed on Monday as technology companies recovered part of the ground they lost last week. In our data, the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ rose 1.2% and Amazon rose about 5%.
why: After a big drop, prices often bounce back a little as some investors buy at lower prices. A bounce does not mean the slide is over, and a drop does not mean it will keep going. It shows how quickly the mood in the market can change.

title: GE Aerospace reports strong quarter, raises outlook
summary: GE Aerospace shared third quarter results on October 20. Orders grew 49% to $19.0 billion, adjusted revenue rose 18% to $13.3 billion, and adjusted earnings per share reached $2.25. The company said it is raising its 2026 guidance across the board.
why: A company's guidance is its own forecast for the year. Raising it is usually good news. But the stock still fell 3.7% in our data, which shows that prices depend on what investors hoped for, not only on the results.

title: Fed chair's speech makes a rate hike this month less likely
summary: Speaking at the IMF meetings in Bangkok, the Fed chair gave no clear signal about future rate moves. Afterward, traders cut the odds of a hike at the October 27 and 28 meeting to under 15%, down from about 27%.
why: The Fed sets short term interest rates. Higher rates make borrowing cost more and can slow company profits, so stocks often wobble when traders expect a hike. The meeting is the next big date to watch.

title: 10 year Treasury yield stays near 5.1%
summary: The yield on the 10 year US Treasury note ended last week near 5.12%. That is a bit lower than earlier in October, when it hit its highest level since 2002.
why: A Treasury is a loan to the US government, and the yield is the interest it pays. When safe bonds pay more, stocks have to look more attractive to compete, so high yields can pull stock prices down.

title: Lockheed Martin sets its third quarter report for Thursday
summary: Lockheed Martin announced that it will release third quarter earnings before the stock market opens on October 22, followed by a call with investors at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. The stock closed Tuesday at $548.71.
why: Every three months a company reports how much it sold and earned. If the numbers or the outlook differ from what analysts expected, the stock can jump or drop quickly, so report days are often the bumpiest.

title: Meta reports third quarter results tonight
summary: Earnings calendars list Meta for Wednesday, October 21, after the market closes, with an investor call at 4:30 p.m. Eastern. Analysts are expecting a big jump in profit compared with a weak quarter a year ago.
why: A quarterly report shows how much a company really sold and earned. Stocks often move a lot the next morning if the numbers or the outlook differ from what analysts guessed.

title: Dow climbs while AI stocks stay under pressure
summary: On Tuesday the Dow rose about 1% to 52,495.88 and the S&P 500 added about 0.3%, helped by good company earnings and lower oil prices. The Nasdaq ended nearly flat after worries about the AI trade.
why: An index is a basket of many companies, so its move shows the mood of the market. Falling oil prices can lower costs for many businesses, but some investors are still unsure if AI spending will pay off.

title: Nasdaq rebounds as investors return to chip stocks
summary: On Monday the Nasdaq rose about 1.1% to 26,430.89 as buyers came back to chip and other AI related companies after a rough week before.
why: When many chip stocks rise together, it often means investors feel more confident about AI demand. One strong day does not guarantee a trend, so it helps to watch several days.

title: Lockheed Martin posts record backlog
summary: Lockheed Martin said sales grew 11% to about $20.7 billion in the third quarter. Its backlog, the pile of signed orders still to be filled, reached a record $292 billion, helped by a large multi year missile interceptor award.
why: A backlog tells you how much work a company already has lined up. A bigger one can mean steadier sales in coming years, though the stock price can still move for other reasons.

title: Meta grows sales 26% but a legal charge hits profit
summary: Meta reported third quarter sales of about $64.6 billion, a quarter more than last year. A one time charge tied to an agreement with state attorneys general made its operating profit shrink, and spending on computers and data centers stayed very high.
why: Sales growing fast is good news, but investors also look at profit and at how much cash is going out. A one time cost is different from everyday costs, so it helps to read both numbers.

title: The 10 year Treasury rate hits a 12 month high
summary: Data from Alpha Vantage show the 10 year Treasury yield averaged 4.99% in September, up from 4.68% in August and 4.06% a year ago.
why: The 10 year rate is what the government pays to borrow for ten years. When it rises, new bonds pay more, and some investors move money away from riskier stocks.

title: Lockheed Martin stock jumps 7% on its results
summary: Lockheed Martin closed up about 7% at $589.91 after it reported quarterly sales of $20.7 billion, up 11%. Its backlog, the orders it has not delivered yet, reached a record $292 billion, helped by a large award for PAC-3 interceptor missiles. The company also updated its outlook for the year.
why: A backlog is like a long list of paid orders waiting to be filled, so it gives a company steady work for years. That is why investors liked the news, but one good day does not guarantee future results.

title: Tech leads a sharp drop in US stocks
summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell about 2.6% and the S&P 500 about 1.2%, according to market reports, while the Dow barely moved. Our own price data agrees, with the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) down 2.9% and the S&P 500 fund (SPY) down 1.2%. Technology and communication companies fell the most.
why: When the biggest tech names drop, the index funds that hold them drop too, even if you own no single tech stock. This is one reason spreading money across different kinds of companies matters.

title: AI chip and equipment stocks slide together
summary: Prices at the close show AMD down 8.1%, Vertiv down 7.8%, TSMC down 4.5%, Nvidia down 4.4% and Broadcom down 4.3%. Market reports link the drop to renewed worry about how much money is going into AI and who will pay for it.
why: These companies make the chips and equipment that AI needs, so they often move as a group. If investors doubt that AI spending will keep growing, the whole group can fall at once.

title: Meta falls 7% a day after its report
summary: Meta closed at $648.85, down 7.0%, the day after sharing quarterly results. Sales grew about 26%, but reports say investors were uneasy about how much the company is spending on AI and what that does to its cash.
why: A company can sell more and still see its stock fall if people worry the spending will not pay off. Watching cash left over after spending, called free cash flow, helps explain moves like this.

title: Dividend and health stocks rise as tech falls
summary: The dividend fund SCHD gained 2.1% and closed at $35.40, near its 52 week high. Eli Lilly rose 2.8% and Intuitive Surgical 3.7%, while health care was one of the few sectors in the green.
why: Different kinds of companies do not always move together. On days when tech falls, steadier areas like dividend payers and health care can hold up, which is the idea behind diversification.

title: Big tech earnings season is close
summary: Calendar sites list Microsoft and Alphabet as expected to report around October 27 or 28, and Amazon around October 29. The companies had not yet confirmed those dates in the sources found, and the sites disagree by a day.
why: When a company reports earnings, it shows how much it sold and earned. Stocks can jump or drop a lot that day, and the results of the biggest companies can move the whole market, so it helps to know the dates are coming.
source: Blofin earnings calendar (dates not confirmed by companies)

title: Intel plans to share results on October 29
summary: Intel says it will publish its third quarter results after the market closes on Thursday, October 29. Intel is not on our list, but it is a large chip company.
why: Chip companies often move together. A report from a big name like Intel can shift how investors feel about chip stocks such as Nvidia or AMD, even when the news is not about them.

title: Stocks end a rocky week a little lower
summary: The S&P 500 fund SPY slipped about half a percent on Friday and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ finished almost flat. Reports on the day pointed to worries about how much companies are spending on AI and what it costs to borrow money. Investors are also waiting for a Federal Reserve decision next week.
why: When a market falls a little after a big drop, it can mean investors are still nervous but not panicking. Beginners can learn from this that a few calm days do not always mean the worry is over.

title: Oil jumps and many stocks drop on Thursday
summary: CNBC reported that the Dow fell by more than 600 points on Thursday as oil prices rose and the sell-off hit most parts of the market. It was the day tech stocks took their biggest one-day fall in months.
why: Oil is used to make gasoline and ship goods, so higher oil prices can raise costs for many companies and for families. When costs go up, investors sometimes expect smaller profits and sell stocks.

title: GE Aerospace beats estimates but its stock still falls
summary: GE Aerospace reported third quarter profit of $2.25 per share, above the roughly $2.01 analysts expected, and raised its 2026 profit forecast to $8.00 to $8.10 per share. The stock still fell, because the fourth quarter outlook looked a bit lower than analysts hoped and cash flow dipped.
why: A stock price reflects what investors expect in the future, not only what just happened. A good report can still disappoint if people were hoping for even more.

title: A big week ahead: the Fed and big tech earnings
summary: Alphabet says it will report its third quarter results on October 28. Reports say Microsoft and Amazon also report in the coming days, and the Federal Reserve is expected to keep interest rates steady at its meeting on Wednesday.
why: Earnings reports show whether a company is really making money, and the Fed's rate decision changes the cost of borrowing for everyone. Both can move prices fast, so many investors watch this week closely.
source: Main Street (Alphabet date) and Reuters (Fed outlook)

title: Lockheed Martin reports record backlog
summary: Lockheed Martin said its third quarter sales grew about 11% to $20.7 billion. Its backlog, the pile of signed orders still to be built, hit a record $292.0 billion, and $52.5 billion of that comes from a long missile interceptor contract. The company also updated its outlook for the year.
why: A backlog is like a long line of customers who already paid or promised to pay. A bigger line can mean steady business for years, but it does not guarantee the stock price will go up.

title: GE Aerospace raises its yearly profit goal
summary: GE Aerospace reported third quarter revenue up 16% to $14.1 billion and said it now expects adjusted profit of $8.00 to $8.10 per share this year, higher than its earlier range. Demand for engines and for repair services is a big reason.
why: When a company raises its goal, it is telling investors business is going better than planned. Even so, the stock fell on Friday, which shows prices also depend on what investors already expected.

title: Big tech reports earnings this week
summary: Earnings calendars show Alphabet and Microsoft reporting on October 28 and Amazon on October 29. Analysts expect Alphabet to earn about $3.03 per share and Microsoft about $4.71 per share.
why: Earnings reports show how much money a company really made. Prices can move a lot when the real numbers are better or worse than the guesses, so this week may feel bumpy.

title: Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday, Amazon Thursday
summary: Earnings calendars show Alphabet and Microsoft reporting on October 28 and Amazon on October 29. Analysts expect Alphabet to earn about $3.03 per share and Microsoft about $4.71 per share. Amazon is expected to earn about $1.97 per share.
why: Earnings reports show how much money a company really made. Prices can move a lot when the real numbers are better or worse than the guesses, so the next few days may feel bumpy.

title: The Fed meets this week, decision Wednesday
summary: The Federal Reserve holds its policy meeting on October 27 and 28, with the interest rate decision due Wednesday afternoon. This meeting does not come with new economic forecasts. Alphabet and Microsoft also report earnings on Wednesday.
why: The Fed sets the cost of borrowing money. When borrowing gets cheaper or more expensive, many stocks move together, so a day with a Fed decision and big earnings can feel bumpy.

title: Chip and AI supplier stocks climb on Monday
summary: NVIDIA closed up 2.4%, AMD up 2.8%, Broadcom up 2.3% and Vertiv up 2.8%. The Nasdaq technology group gained about 1.0% on average, according to market data from Financial Modeling Prep.
why: Companies that supply parts for AI often move together because they depend on the same big customers. One good day is a data point, not a trend, and these stocks can swing a lot both ways.

title: The Federal Reserve decides on interest rates Wednesday
summary: The Fed's policy committee meets on October 27 and 28. Its decision is due Wednesday at 2:00 PM Eastern time, followed by a press conference at 2:30 PM. Stocks rose on Tuesday as investors waited for the news.
why: Interest rates are the price of borrowing money. When rates change, or when the Fed hints at what comes next, prices of many stocks can move at once, especially fast growing companies.

title: Wall Street climbs as oil eases and AI hopes hold
summary: US stocks rose on Tuesday, with technology leading and chip companies strong. Reuters reported that cooling oil prices and optimism about AI helped lift the mood before the Fed decision.
why: When oil gets cheaper, costs for many businesses and families can ease. Strong AI news tends to lift the companies that build the chips and equipment behind it.

title: Broadcom reportedly seeks more than $60 billion in debt for AI chips
summary: Reports citing Bloomberg say Broadcom is talking with lenders about raising more than $60 billion. The money would help pay for AI chips that Anthropic and other customers would use. The talks were not a finished deal in the reports we found.
why: It shows how much money is going into AI equipment. It also shows that the companies building it are borrowing heavily, which adds risk if demand slows.

title: The Fed announces its interest rate decision today
summary: The Federal Reserve's policy committee meets on October 27 and 28. It shares its decision at 2:00 PM Eastern time today, with a press conference after. The result was not known when we wrote this.
why: Interest rates are the price of borrowing money. When the Fed changes rates, or hints at what is next, prices of many stocks can move at once, especially fast growing companies.

title: Lockheed Martin lifts its yearly forecast after a strong quarter
summary: Lockheed reported third quarter sales of about $20.7 billion, up 11%, and said its order backlog hit a record near $292 billion. It also raised its profit outlook for the year. Its stock rose on the news.
why: A backlog is work customers have already ordered but the company has not finished. A bigger backlog gives a company steady future sales, which helps calm the ride for owners.

title: Meta stock drops about 7% after its quarterly report
summary: Meta's sales grew about 26% to roughly $64.6 billion. Even so, its stock fell about 7% as investors worried about how much it will spend on AI. Many analysts still raised their price targets.
why: Good sales do not always lift a stock. If a company spends a lot on new projects, investors may fear lower profits for a while. This shows why price depends on expectations, not just results.

title: The Fed keeps interest rates unchanged, with two votes for a hike
summary: The Federal Reserve left its main interest rate in a range of 3.75% to 4% on October 28. Two members of the committee wanted to raise it by a quarter point. Reports say the Fed's chair also announced that it will hold fewer rate-setting meetings starting in 2027.
why: Interest rates are the price of borrowing money. Rates staying put is calmer than a surprise, but two votes for a hike show some officials worry about prices rising too fast. Higher rates can weigh on fast growing companies, so stocks may stay jumpy.

title: Vertiv sales jump 61% and the company raises its yearly forecast
summary: Vertiv, which makes the power and cooling equipment that keeps data centers running, reported third quarter sales of $4.31 billion, up 61% from a year earlier. Its new orders more than doubled, and it raised its outlook for the full year. The stock closed up about 16% on the day.
why: AI needs huge buildings full of computers, and those buildings need power and cooling. Vertiv sells those parts, so strong sales hint that AI building is still speeding up. Even so, the stock is still far below its 52 week high, and big one day jumps can fade.

title: Microsoft's cloud business speeds up to 48% growth
summary: Microsoft said total sales were about $92.3 billion, up 19%, and that its Azure cloud service grew 48%. That beat the company's own forecast and the 42% growth of the last quarter. Reports say the stock rose about 4% in after hours trading.
why: Azure rents out computer power over the internet, and AI needs a lot of it. Faster growth suggests companies are still spending on AI. Still, after hours moves can fade by the next day.

title: Alphabet's sales climb 25% to about $127.6 billion
summary: Alphabet, the company behind Google and YouTube, said its third quarter sales rose 25% from a year earlier. Profit per share was $2.12. The report came out after the market closed on Wednesday.
why: Sales growth of 25% is fast for such a giant company. Whether the stock rises will depend on how the report compares with what investors expected, and on how much Alphabet plans to spend on AI.

title: Alphabet stock has its biggest one day drop after earnings
summary: Alphabet shares fell about 12.6% on Thursday after its third quarter report. Reports say profit per share came in at $2.12, below the $3.02 analysts expected, while spending on AI equipment was larger than the cash the business produced. Its cloud unit grew very fast.
why: When a company spends more than it earns in cash, investors worry about how long that can last. Even a great cloud business did not calm that worry, and a big drop like this shows how much a stock can move on one report.

title: Amazon's cloud speeds up to 39% growth, but spending worries linger
summary: Amazon reported after the close that its AWS cloud unit grew 39% from a year ago, its fastest pace in nearly five years. Profit per share of $1.89 was a little under what analysts expected. Reports disagree on how far the stock fell in after hours trading.
why: AWS rents out computer power, which AI needs a lot of, so faster growth is a good sign. But Amazon is also spending huge sums on new data centers, and investors are watching whether that spending pays off.

title: Eli Lilly raises its yearly sales forecast after a strong quarter
summary: Eli Lilly said third quarter sales rose 39% to $24.4 billion, led by its diabetes and weight loss medicines Mounjaro and Zepbound. It raised its full year sales forecast to $91 billion to $92 billion. The stock rose about 6.6% on Thursday.
why: A company raising its own forecast tells investors it expects to keep selling more. Still, Lilly said it sold more units at lower prices, so it is worth watching whether price cuts slow future profit.

title: The Fed keeps interest rates unchanged in a split vote
summary: The Federal Reserve left its main rate at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday. Two officials voted to raise it by a quarter point, and reports say markets now see a good chance of a hike in December. The 10 year Treasury yield was reported near 5%.
why: Higher interest rates make borrowing cost more and can make safer investments like bonds look more attractive compared with stocks. That is why rate news can move the whole market, especially fast growing tech companies.

title: Amazon posts its best ever operating profit margin
summary: Amazon said its third quarter sales reached $201.9 billion and operating profit was $28.1 billion, about 13.9% of sales. The cloud unit AWS made $46.0 billion in sales. For the next quarter the company expects sales of $240 billion to $247 billion.
why: Operating margin is how many cents of profit a company keeps from each dollar of sales. A higher margin means the business is getting better at turning sales into profit. Still, the stock fell before the report, which shows investors also worry about how much Amazon spends on AI.

title: Meta narrows its AI spending plan but cash turns negative
summary: Meta said it expects to spend between $135 billion and $145 billion this year on equipment like data centers. In the third quarter it spent about $34.9 billion, which was more than the cash its business produced. It also set aside a large one time charge for legal cases.
why: Spending more than you earn in cash is fine for a while if it builds something that pays off later, but it is a risk if it does not. This is the same question investors are asking about Alphabet and Amazon, so Meta is a good example to follow.
source: Let's Data Science, citing Meta's report

title: Tech sell-off drags down the Nasdaq on the last trading day of October
summary: Stocks fell sharply on Friday as investors worried about how much money tech companies are spending on AI. News reports say the Nasdaq Composite lost close to 3% and the S&P 500 about 1.8%, leaving the Nasdaq roughly 8% below its early October peak. It was the Nasdaq's worst month since March 2025.
why: When big companies spend a lot on AI, investors ask when that spending will turn into profit. If they doubt it, they sell, and many tech stocks fall together. This is why owning different kinds of companies can soften a bad day.

title: Eli Lilly beats expectations and raises its 2026 sales outlook
summary: Lilly said third quarter revenue grew 39% to $24.4 billion, led by its Mounjaro and Zepbound medicines. It raised its full year sales forecast to a range of $91 billion to $92 billion. About $900 million of the quarter came from one time items.
why: Beating expectations and raising the outlook tells investors the business is growing faster than planned. Reading the fine print matters too, because one time gains do not repeat every quarter.

title: Chip and AI supplier stocks fall harder than the AI giants
summary: AMD lost nearly 11% and Broadcom, TSMC and Vertiv each fell more than 5% on Friday, based on closing prices from our data provider. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta fell about 1.4% to 1.6%. Reports tied the day's mood to weak tech earnings and worry about AI costs.
why: Companies that sell chips and equipment for AI do well when everyone is spending and are hit hard when people worry that spending will slow. Bigger companies with many products usually move less.

title: AMD sets its third quarter report for Tuesday after the close
summary: AMD said it will release fiscal third quarter results on Tuesday, November 3, after the market closes, with a call at 5 p.m. Eastern. Last quarter the company told investors to expect about $13 billion in sales for this period, plus or minus $300 million.
why: Earnings reports are when a company shows its real results. If the numbers beat what people hoped for, the stock can jump; if they fall short, it can drop, even when the business is growing. That is why prices often swing around these dates.

title: The Fed's next meeting is December 8 and 9
summary: The Federal Reserve's official calendar shows its next policy meeting on December 8 and 9, with a decision at 2 p.m. Eastern on the second day and a news conference after. Minutes from that meeting are due December 30.
why: The Fed sets a key interest rate that affects loans, savings and how much investors will pay for stocks. Rate hopes and worries move the market in the weeks before each meeting, so it helps to know the date.

title: Rocket Lab's last report set a sales goal for this quarter
summary: In its August report, Rocket Lab said quarterly sales hit a record $234 million, up 62% from a year earlier. It guided to $250 million to $265 million in sales for the third quarter, with an adjusted loss still expected. The company has not been confirmed to report on a specific November date in our sources.
why: A company's own forecast is a yardstick. When the next report arrives, investors compare real results with that range. A fast growing company that still loses money can swing a lot, which fits Rocket Lab's high risk score.

title: AMD shares its third quarter results today after the close
summary: AMD said it would report third quarter results on Tuesday, November 3, after the market closes, with a call at 5 p.m. Eastern. In its last report the company said it expected about $13 billion in sales this quarter, give or take $300 million.
why: A company's own forecast is a yardstick. When the real numbers come out, investors compare them with that range and with what they hoped for. A stock can fall even on good results if people hoped for more, so a big move in either direction is possible.

title: The 10 year Treasury yield eased to 4.91%
summary: Treasury data show the 10 year yield closed Monday at 4.91%, down from 5.05% on October 28. The yield is the interest rate the government pays to borrow money for ten years.
why: This rate is like a price tag on money. When it falls, safer investments pay a bit less, so investors may feel more comfortable owning stocks, especially fast growing ones. When it rises, the opposite can happen.
source: U.S. Treasury daily yield curve rates

title: The Treasury announces how much it plans to borrow on Wednesday
summary: The U.S. Treasury is scheduled to announce its quarterly refunding plan on Wednesday, November 4. This tells the market how much government debt it plans to sell in the coming months.
why: When the government sells more bonds, it can push interest rates up, because buyers want to be paid for taking on more supply. Rates matter to every stock, so people watch this announcement closely.

title: Tech was the weakest part of the Nasdaq on Monday
summary: Sector data for the Nasdaq show technology companies fell about 3.5% on average on Monday, while consumer defensive companies, which sell everyday products, rose about 2.4%. On our list AMD fell 7.5% and Microsoft fell 2.8%.
why: Stocks in the same industry often move together, so a bad day for one can pull others down. That is why spreading money across different kinds of businesses can make a rough day feel smaller.

title: Tech and AI related stocks bounced back on Tuesday
summary: After a rough Monday, several big technology and AI related companies climbed. Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Microsoft, Meta, Nvidia and Amazon all gained between about 2% and 5%. Across Nasdaq companies, tech rose about 0.9% and industrial firms rose about 1.6%.
why: Stocks that rise and fall together are tied to the same story, here the excitement around AI. A rebound after a drop is normal, but it does not mean the worry is over. It is a reminder that prices of fast growing companies swing a lot.
source: Financial Modeling Prep sector performance and quotes

title: The 10 year Treasury yield rose to 4.95%
summary: The interest rate on 10 year U.S. government bonds ticked up from 4.91% on Monday to 4.95% on Tuesday. It remains lower than the 5.05% seen on October 28.
why: The 10 year yield is like the price of borrowing money for a long time. When it goes up, new bonds pay more, so stocks have to look more attractive to compete. Fast growing companies are often the most sensitive to this.
source: U.S. Treasury daily yield curve rates

title: AMD reports third quarter sales above its guide
summary: AMD shared third quarter results after the market closed on Tuesday. A summary of its company filing says sales were $13.4 billion, higher than the roughly $13 billion it had forecast in August. Its profit per share, adjusted for one time items, was $2.09.
why: Companies give forecasts called guidance. Beating your own forecast is a good sign, but the stock price depends on whether investors hoped for even more, so the move at the open can go either way. The full report was not opened, so check the company page for details.

title: Vertiv reports big sales growth, then falls sharply a week later
summary: A summary of Vertiv's company filing says third quarter sales were $4.3 billion, up 61% from a year earlier, and that the company raised its outlook for the full year. On November 4 the stock closed down 12.9%. We could not confirm what caused today's drop.
why: A company can do very well and its stock can still fall if investors hoped for more or worry about the future. This is why the price reaction matters as much as the report itself.

title: The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October
summary: Monthly data shows the average yield on 10 year U.S. government bonds rose to 5.13% in October. A year earlier it was 4.06%, and the 12 month low was 4.09% in November 2025.
why: A bond yield is the interest you earn for lending money to the government. When it rises, safe bonds look better and stocks, especially expensive ones, can lose some appeal.

title: Stocks rally broadly after the US midterm elections
summary: US stocks rose sharply on Wednesday, with Microsoft and Amazon each up about 6% and the Nasdaq leading. Several market reports tie the move to relief now that the election result is known, though sources disagree on the exact index numbers.
why: Markets do not like surprises. When a big unknown gets settled, investors often buy. But rallies fueled by relief can fade fast, so one good day does not tell you what comes next.

title: The Treasury announces how much it plans to borrow
summary: The US Treasury published its borrowing plan on Wednesday. The amount of government borrowing can affect how much interest the government has to offer on its bonds.
why: If the government sells more bonds, it may have to pay higher interest to attract buyers. Higher bond rates can make stocks look less attractive by comparison.

title: S&P 500 drops 4.4% in its worst day since April 2025
summary: A sharp sell-off in AI stocks pulled the whole US market down on Thursday. The S&P 500 fell 4.4%, its biggest one day drop since the tariff shock of April 2025, just a day after Wednesday's rally.
why: The S&P 500 is a list of 500 big US companies, so when it falls this much, almost every stock and most index funds fall too. Big drops like this feel scary, but they happen from time to time, and what matters is your time horizon.

title: Dow plunges about 1,800 points as Nasdaq enters a correction
summary: Yahoo Finance's live market coverage describes an AI trade meltdown on Thursday. The Dow lost roughly 1,800 points and the tech heavy Nasdaq fell into what traders call a correction.
why: A correction means a market index has dropped at least 10% from its recent high. It is a normal, if uncomfortable, part of investing, and the stocks that rose the most before often fall the most.

title: CNN ties the AI sell-off to the US midterm election results
summary: CNN reports that the midterm election results sent the AI trade into a tailspin, even though stocks had rallied the day before. Other outlets also point to worries about how much companies are spending on AI.
why: News can move prices in surprising ways, and the first explanation is not always the whole story. Reporters and analysts often disagree, so treat any single reason with care.

title: October jobs report lands this morning
summary: The government releases its monthly jobs report at 8:30 a.m. New York time today. Economists surveyed by CNBC expected only about 59,000 new jobs, a small number. Traders are also watching to see how the numbers shape the Fed's next move.
why: The jobs report shows how many people got hired last month. The Fed uses it to decide whether to raise, hold or lower interest rates. Rates matter because they change how much big, fast growing companies are worth to investors, so a surprise in either direction can move the whole market.

title: Fed keeps rates steady, but two officials wanted a hike
summary: The Federal Reserve left its main interest rate at 3.75% to 4% on October 28. The vote was 10 to 2. Two members would have raised it by a quarter of a point, and the Fed said inflation is still elevated.
why: The Fed is the group that sets the cost of borrowing money in the US. When some members want higher rates, it hints that rates could go up instead of down. Higher rates make safe bonds more attractive and can make stocks, especially expensive tech stocks, look less appealing.

title: Nasdaq falls 5.5% as AI chip stocks lead the drop
summary: The Nasdaq, an index full of tech companies, dropped 5.5% on Thursday and moved into what traders call correction territory. Chip makers were hit hardest. Market writers linked the fall to worries about AI rules and spending after the midterm elections.
why: A correction means prices have fallen about 10% or more from a recent high. Chip companies sell the parts that power AI, so when investors worry about AI, these stocks often move more than the rest of the market. It is also why owning many different kinds of companies can soften the bumps.

title: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October; unemployment at 4.1%
summary: The government's monthly jobs count came in stronger than many analysts expected. Unemployment stayed low at 4.1%. The report was the big event for markets on Friday.
why: When more people have jobs, the economy looks healthy, which is good. But it can also mean the Fed keeps interest rates high for longer, and high rates tend to weigh on growth stocks. That is why a strong report can make the market nervous.

title: Chip stocks bounce back after a hard fall
summary: Shares of chip companies rose on Friday after a sharp drop the day before. AMD gained about 11%. Reports said the bounce won back part of the earlier losses, but analysts warned that prices could keep swinging.
why: When a group of stocks falls fast and then jumps, it is often investors catching their breath, not a sign of what comes next. For a beginner, the lesson is that big one day moves in both directions are normal for chip stocks, so check how far a stock still is from its high before getting excited.

title: US stocks rise on Friday but the week still ends lower
summary: The S&P 500 gained about 0.3% and the Nasdaq about 1.1% on Friday, a partial recovery from the day before. The Dow slipped slightly. Reports said worries about tighter rules for the AI industry had hit stocks earlier in the week.
why: The S&P 500 is a basket of 500 big US companies, so it shows the mood of the whole market. A small gain after a big drop means the market is still nervous. It helps to look at a whole week, not just one day.

title: Strong jobs report pushes Treasury yields higher
summary: Reports said October's job gains were stronger than expected, and that this lifted Treasury yields and the odds that interest rates stay high or rise. Higher yields give investors a safe alternative to stocks.
why: When the government pays more interest on its bonds, stocks have to look better to compete. Fast growing tech companies are hit the most, because their profits are expected far in the future and high rates make future money worth less today.

title: Wall Street rebounds from last week's slump
summary: Stocks rose sharply on Monday, with the Dow up roughly 1,100 points and the Nasdaq up about 3%. The rally followed a hard drop after the midterm elections. Tech shares led the rebound.
why: After a big fall, stocks often bounce as investors calm down. A bounce is not proof that the worst is over, so beginners should look at the bigger trend, not one day.

title: Oil prices slide, easing inflation worries
summary: Oil fell after the U.S. president said on Sunday that fresh attacks on Iran were highly unlikely. Cheaper oil can mean lower costs for companies and families.
why: When oil gets cheaper, prices for many things can rise more slowly. That makes it easier for interest rates to stay lower, which is good news for stocks.

title: NVIDIA falls while other chip makers jump
summary: NVIDIA shares dropped on reports about its chief executive, while rivals like AMD and Broadcom rose more than 7%. NVIDIA was the only one of the big seven tech companies to lose ground.
why: News about one company can push its stock down even on a day when the whole market rises. This is why owning many different companies is safer than betting on one.

title: AI chip suppliers bounce hard
summary: AMD, Broadcom and Vertiv posted some of the biggest gains on our list. They had fallen sharply in recent days, so part of the move may be investors buying back in.
why: Stocks that rise 10% in a day can fall 10% just as fast. A big jump is exciting, but it also shows how risky these companies can be.

title: Inflation report due before the market opens
summary: The government is scheduled to publish its October consumer price report at 8:30 a.m. Eastern today. It shows how fast everyday prices are rising.
why: Prices rising fast can push interest rates higher, and higher rates often hurt growth stocks. A calmer number can help stocks. Nobody knows the result until it comes out.

title: NVIDIA sets its earnings call for November 17
summary: NVIDIA announced it will report results for the quarter that ended October 25 on Tuesday, November 17. The conference call starts at 5 p.m. Eastern.
why: Earnings reports are when a company shows its real sales and profit. Stocks often move a lot that day, so it is a good date to watch if you want to learn how earnings work.

title: October inflation comes in hotter than expected
summary: The government's consumer price report showed prices rose 0.4% in October, more than the 0.3% that economists had predicted. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3%. Housing costs were the biggest reason for the increase.
why: When prices rise quickly, the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates to cool things down. Higher rates make loans more expensive and often push stock prices lower, especially for tech companies whose big profits are expected far in the future.

title: A December rate hike looks more likely
summary: After the inflation report, news coverage said the Federal Reserve is now very likely to raise its key interest rate at its December meeting. One Fed governor had said a bigger half point hike should be considered if core prices rose 0.3% or more, which they did.
why: The Fed's interest rate affects almost everything, from savings accounts to car loans to how much investors are willing to pay for stocks. That is why the whole market pays close attention to every hint about what the Fed will do next.

title: NVIDIA drops again as questions swirl around its CEO
summary: NVIDIA shares fell for a second straight day after news reports raised concerns about CEO Jensen Huang and possible chip sales linked to China. The company's board opened an independent review, and a member of Congress said he may demand that the CEO answer questions.
why: This is an example of key person risk: worries about one leader can pull down a huge company's stock even when its products have not changed. It also shows that news about rules and politics can matter as much as sales numbers.

title: Rocket Lab reports record quarterly sales
summary: Rocket Lab said it brought in $268 million in its third quarter, its highest ever and 73% more than a year earlier. Its backlog, meaning work customers have already ordered but not yet received, grew to about $3.6 billion.
why: A growing backlog is like a long list of future paychecks, so it can make investors more confident. But Rocket Lab still swings a lot, so one strong report does not remove the risk.

title: Stocks trade today, but the bond market takes a holiday
summary: Wall Street's stock exchanges are open for regular hours on Veterans Day. The bond market is closed, following the guidance of the bond industry group SIFMA, and most banks are closed too.
why: When part of the market is closed, fewer people are trading. That can make prices move in odd ways, so one quiet day is not a strong signal about where stocks are headed.

title: Nasdaq ends lower as inflation worries return
summary: Tech heavy stocks fell on Tuesday after a report showed prices rising faster than expected. Investors worried that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates, and chip stocks like NVIDIA led the drop.
why: Interest rates act like gravity for stock prices. When people expect higher rates, they often pay less for fast growing companies, which is why QQQ fell more than SPY.

title: Broadcom keeps climbing after a big Monday
summary: Broadcom rose about 3.9% on Tuesday, after jumping close to 9% on Monday. The company has set December 9 as the date it will share its next quarterly results.
why: A results date gives investors a day to circle on the calendar. Stocks can rise before results when people expect good news, but they can also fall fast if the results disappoint.

title: CoreWeave results spark a rebound in AI chip stocks
summary: CoreWeave, a company that rents out computing power for AI, said its sales grew about 168% from a year earlier and raised its forecast for 2026. It also said its backlog, meaning work customers have already signed up for, is now above $130 billion. Chip and AI equipment stocks rose the next day.
why: CoreWeave buys huge numbers of AI chips. When a big buyer says demand is still strong, investors feel better about the companies that make those chips. It helped calm worries that AI spending is slowing down.

title: Baird lowers its rating on NVIDIA
summary: The research firm Baird moved NVIDIA to Neutral and cut its price target to $200. It pointed to slower AI spending, limits on supply and uncertainty about the CEO's future. NVIDIA's stock still rose that day along with other chip stocks.
why: A rating cut is one expert's opinion that the stock may not do as well as hoped. It is worth knowing, but other analysts may disagree. NVIDIA's own results on November 17 will give much more real information.

title: Microsoft falls as Anthropic launches office tools
summary: Microsoft shares dropped after the AI company Anthropic announced new workplace tools, including ones for spreadsheets and meetings. Investors worry these could compete with Microsoft Office and its Copilot assistant.
why: Office software brings Microsoft a lot of steady money. When a new rival appears, investors ask if that money could shrink, and the price can fall even before any customers switch.

title: Tech groups push back on a proposed China parts ban
summary: Microsoft and industry groups asked the government to rethink a proposed ban on certain Chinese-made optical parts used in AI data centers. These parts help move data quickly between computers.
why: If a key part gets banned, companies may have to find new suppliers, which can cost more and slow down building data centers. Rules from governments can affect a company's costs.

title: AI stocks lead Wall Street higher while others lag
summary: The broad stock market rose on Wednesday, led by a rebound in AI related stocks after a rough week. Many stocks outside of AI did not join in, and the Dow was roughly flat for much of the day.
why: When only one group of stocks drives the market, the gains rest on fewer shoulders. That is why owning a mix of different kinds of companies, called diversification, matters.

title: NVIDIA's board meets on the CEO's future
summary: NVIDIA's board of directors met late Wednesday to discuss whether Jensen Huang should stay on as CEO, according to reports citing people familiar with the talks. This follows his admission to staff over the weekend about his personal life and an outside investigation led by a law firm. No decision had been announced by Thursday morning.
why: Jensen Huang has led NVIDIA since he helped start it in 1993, and many investors see him as central to its success. Not knowing who will lead a company makes investors nervous, even when the business itself is doing well.

title: NVIDIA slides before the open and pulls futures lower
summary: NVIDIA shares fell more than 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday and were still down about 6% to 7% early Thursday. Futures for the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 pointed lower. NVIDIA is one of the largest companies in both indexes.
why: When one giant company falls, index funds like SPY and QQQ feel it too, because they hold a lot of that stock. This is why owning one company carries more risk than owning many.

title: AMD and Broadcom rise as NVIDIA stumbles
summary: After the NVIDIA reports came out, shares of AMD and Broadcom each rose more than 3% in after hours trading. Both make chips that compete with NVIDIA's in AI data centers. Some investors appear to be moving money toward these rivals.
why: When one company has trouble, its competitors can benefit, because customers and investors may look elsewhere. Moves outside regular hours can change a lot once the full market opens.

title: AMD jumps after an upbeat analyst note
summary: AMD closed up 7.3% at $552.90 on Wednesday. Strong results from CoreWeave, a big buyer of AI chips, helped, and a UBS analyst note said AMD is holding its share of the computer processor market while Intel's share slipped.
why: Market share means how much of all sales in an industry go to one company. Gaining or keeping share against a rival is a sign a company's products are competitive.

title: Another price report is due Friday
summary: After a hotter than expected consumer inflation report on Tuesday, the next big data point is the producer price index on Friday. It tracks the prices businesses pay for goods and services. Economists expect it to show prices still rising faster than the Federal Reserve wants.
why: Prices businesses pay often get passed on to shoppers later. If this report is hot, the Fed may be more likely to raise interest rates in December, which can weigh on stocks.
